As a result, any class in the package can access these inner classes. The enclosing class's private fields become protected fields, accessible by the now external 'inner class'.

CodeIssue.Title: Class Contains Inner Class
CodeIssue.Description: When translated into bytecode, any inner classes are rebuilt within the JVM as external classes within the same package. As a result, any class in the package can access these inner classes. The enclosing class's private fields become protected fields, accessible by the now external 'inner class'.

As a result, any class in the package can access these inner classes. The enclosing class's private fields become protected fields, accessible by the now external 'inner class'.

As a result, any class in the package can access these inner classes. The enclosing class's private fields become protected fields, accessible by the now external 'inner class'.

CodeIssue.Title: Class Contains Inner Class
CodeIssue.Description: When translated into bytecode, any inner classes are rebuilt within the JVM as external classes within the same package. As a result, any class in the package can access these inner classes. The enclosing class's private fields become protected fields, accessible by the now external 'inner class'.

As a result, any class in the package can access these inner classes. The enclosing class's private fields become protected fields, accessible by the now external 'inner class'.

CodeIssue.Title: java.io.File
CodeIssue.Description: This functionality acts as an entry point for external data and the code should be manually checked to ensure the data obtained is correctly validated and/or sanitised. Additionally, carefull checks/sanitisation should be applied in any situation where the user may be able to control or affect the filename.
